paragraphs.title: Integrity, Humility, and the Consequences of Wickedness

easy.explanation: The verse says, “A false balance is abomination to the LORD.”
easy.q: What is an abomination to the LORD according to verse 1?

easy.explanation: Proverbs 11:2 says, “When pride cometh, then cometh shame.”
easy.q: What comes when pride comes?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “The integrity of the upright shall guide them.”
easy.q: What shall guide the upright?

answers: Deceit versus what pleases the LORD
medium.explanation: A false balance represents deceit, while a just weight is the LORD’s delight.
medium.q: What contrast is made between a false balance and a just weight?

answers: They fall or are destroyed by their wickedness
medium.explanation: The verses repeatedly say that wickedness brings destruction, falling, or being taken in sin.
medium.q: What happens to the wicked according to verses 3–6?

medium.explanation: The lowly are humble people, and the verse connects them with wisdom.
medium.q: What does “lowly” mean in verse 2?

challenge.explanation: Integrity guides the upright, and righteousness delivers from death and trouble.
challenge.q: What common function do integrity and righteousness have in these verses?

answers: Riches are more valuable than integrity
challenge.explanation: Riches profit nothing in the day of wrath, but righteousness delivers from death.
challenge.q: What does verse 4 teach about riches?

answers: Integrity guides and delivers, while wickedness destroys
Pride brings wisdom, and deceit brings honour
Riches guarantee safety, and wickedness brings peace
challenge.explanation: The passage consistently contrasts the safety of righteousness with the ruin of wickedness.
challenge.q: Which sequence best summarizes verses 1–6?

paragraphs.title: The Righteous, the Wicked, and the Welfare of the City

easy.explanation: Verse 7 says, “When a wicked man dieth, his expectation shall perish.”
easy.q: What happens to a wicked man’s expectation when he dies?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “When it goeth well with the righteous, the city rejoiceth.”
easy.q: What happens when it goes well with the righteous?

easy.explanation: A faithful person conceals the matter, while a talebearer reveals secrets.
easy.q: Who conceals a matter?

answers: They cause the city to fall
medium.explanation: The city rejoices at the righteous and is exalted by the blessing of the upright.
medium.q: How do the righteous affect the city according to verses 10–11?

medium.explanation: The verse contrasts the fall of people without counsel with safety in a multitude of counsellors.
medium.q: Why may a people fall when there is no counsel?

medium.explanation: A talebearer is described as one who reveals secrets.
medium.q: What is a “talebearer”?

challenge.explanation: The passage warns about hypocritical, secret-revealing, and harmful speech.
challenge.q: What kind of speech threatens the community in this passage?

answers: The wise person restrains his speech
The wise person despises his neighbour
challenge.explanation: The man of understanding holds his peace, while the person void of wisdom despises his neighbour.
challenge.q: What contrast is made between a person void of wisdom and a man of understanding?

challenge.explanation: Proverbs 11:14 says, “In the multitude of counsellors there is safety.”
challenge.q: What role does counsel play in governing a people?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “He that is surety for a stranger shall smart for it.”
easy.q: What warning is given about being surety for a stranger?

easy.explanation: Proverbs 11:16 says, “A gracious woman retaineth honour.”
easy.q: What does a gracious woman retain?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “The merciful man doeth good to his own soul.”
easy.q: What does the merciful man do to his own soul?

answers: The merciful man does good to himself, while the cruel man troubles himself
The rich man helps the poor, while the poor man rules
The wise man reveals secrets, while the fool conceals them
medium.explanation: Mercy benefits the person who practices it, while cruelty harms the cruel person.
medium.q: What contrast appears in verse 17?

answers: The wicked works deceitfully, while the righteous receives a sure reward
The wicked sows righteousness, while the righteous works deceitfully
medium.explanation: Verse 18 contrasts a deceitful work with the sure reward of righteousness.
medium.q: What is the difference between the wicked man’s work and the work of one who sows righteousness?

answers: A person who guarantees another’s obligation
A person who keeps a secret
medium.explanation: A surety accepts responsibility for another person’s obligation.
medium.q: What does “surety” mean in this passage?

answers: Careless responsibility does not remove accountability
challenge.explanation: The passage warns against reckless guarantees and affirms that evil will not go unpunished.
challenge.q: What can be concluded from the warning about surety and the statement about the wicked?

challenge.explanation: Verse 19 says, “As righteousness tendeth to life.”
challenge.q: How is righteousness related to life?

answers: The wicked will not escape punishment
challenge.explanation: Even united or confident wicked people will not avoid punishment.
challenge.q: What does “hand join in hand” emphasize in verse 21?

answers: A jewel of gold in a swine’s snout
easy.explanation: Verse 22 makes this exact comparison.
easy.q: What is a fair woman without discretion compared to?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “The desire of the righteous is only good.”
easy.q: What is the desire of the righteous?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “The liberal soul shall be made fat.”
easy.q: What happens to the liberal soul?

answers: Outward beauty is always most important
medium.explanation: The comparison shows that beauty is of little value without discretion or character.
medium.q: What does verse 22 teach about outward beauty?

answers: The righteous desire good, while the wicked expect wrath
The righteous expect wrath, while the wicked desire good
medium.explanation: The verse contrasts the good desire of the righteous with the wicked person’s expectation of wrath.
medium.q: What is the difference between the desire of the righteous and the expectation of the wicked?

medium.explanation: The person who refreshes others will himself be refreshed.
medium.q: What does it mean to water others in verse 25?

answers: Inner character matters more than outward appearance
Outward beauty is more important than wisdom
challenge.explanation: The passage values discretion, goodness, and generosity above external appearance.
challenge.q: What principle connects the verse about beauty with the verses about desire and generosity?

answers: The giver is refreshed and blessed
challenge.explanation: The verse promises that the one who waters others will also be watered.
challenge.q: How does generosity affect the giver?

answers: Both are directed toward good and blessing
challenge.explanation: The righteous desire good, and generosity produces refreshment and blessing.
challenge.q: What connection exists between righteous desire and generosity?

paragraphs.title: Social Responsibility and the Pursuit of Good

easy.explanation: The verse says, “The people shall curse him.”
easy.q: What do the people do to the person who withholds corn?

answers: The head of him that selleth corn
The head of one who withholds it
The head of one who trusts in riches
easy.explanation: Blessing rests on the person who supplies or sells the corn.
easy.q: Upon whose head shall blessing be?

answers: They shall flourish as a branch
easy.explanation: Verse 28 says, “The righteous shall flourish as a branch.”
easy.q: What shall happen to the righteous?

answers: It exploits scarcity and harms the people
It causes the righteous to flourish
medium.explanation: The people curse the one who withholds needed food, while blessing belongs to the supplier.
medium.q: Why does the passage condemn withholding corn?

answers: Seeking good procures favour, while mischief comes back upon the seeker
Seeking good leads to falling, while mischief leads to flourishing
medium.explanation: Verse 27 promises favour to the seeker of good and trouble to the seeker of mischief.
medium.q: What is the difference between seeking good and seeking mischief?

answers: Supplies or sells something to others
medium.explanation: The seller provides corn to the people rather than withholding it.
medium.q: What does “selleth” mean in verse 26?

answers: Withholding and harming the public versus supplying and seeking good
challenge.explanation: The passage condemns withholding necessities and praises supplying others and seeking good.
challenge.q: What social contrast appears in verses 26–27?

answers: Trusting in riches can lead to a fall
Riches are more important than righteousness
challenge.explanation: The verse says, “He that trusteth in his riches shall fall.”
challenge.q: What does verse 28 teach about trusting in riches?

answers: The righteous are portrayed as a source of benefit and blessing
The righteous are portrayed as hoarders
The righteous have no relationship to society
challenge.explanation: The surrounding verses connect goodness, provision, blessing, and the flourishing of the righteous.
challenge.q: How is the flourishing of the righteous related to social responsibility?

easy.explanation: Verse 29 says, “He that troubleth his own house shall inherit the wind.”
easy.q: What shall the person who troubles his own house inherit?

easy.explanation: The verse calls the fruit of the righteous “a tree of life.”
easy.q: What is the fruit of the righteous?

easy.explanation: Verse 29 says, “The fool shall be servant to the wise of heart.”
easy.q: Who shall be servant to the wise of heart?

medium.explanation: Inheriting the wind pictures emptiness, while the fool becomes servant to the wise.
medium.q: What is the result of troubling one’s own house?

medium.explanation: The fruit of the righteous is compared to a tree of life.
medium.q: How does the fruit of the righteous benefit people?

medium.explanation: To trouble one’s house is to harm or disturb it.
medium.q: What does “troubleth” mean in “he that troubleth his own house”?

answers: Wisdom and good character are superior to foolishness
Wealth is the only path to growth
challenge.explanation: The fool is placed in servitude to the wise of heart.
challenge.q: What does the contrast between the fool and the wise of heart teach?

answers: Troubling the home brings emptiness, while righteousness brings life
Every action produces the same result
challenge.explanation: The verses present different outcomes according to the character and actions of a person.
challenge.q: How does the passage connect actions with consequences?

answers: If the righteous are recompensed, the wicked will certainly face consequences
The wicked are exempt from consequences
challenge.explanation: The final verse strengthens the certainty that the wicked and sinner will receive according to their deeds.
challenge.q: What does “much more the wicked and the sinner” imply?

easy.explanation: The chapter repeatedly commends righteousness, integrity, kindness, and goodness.
easy.q: Which quality is repeatedly praised throughout the chapter?

easy.explanation: Wickedness is associated with shame, destruction, falling, wrath, and punishment.
easy.q: What does wickedness repeatedly bring?

easy.explanation: The righteous cause the city to rejoice, exalt it, and provide life-giving fruit.
easy.q: What do the righteous bring to those around them?

answers: Integrity and kindness bring blessing, while wickedness brings harmful consequences
Wealth and beauty always bring life
medium.explanation: The chapter repeatedly contrasts the beneficial way of righteousness with the destructive way of wickedness.
medium.q: Which idea best summarizes the chapter?

answers: Words and actions can help or corrupt the community
Society is unaffected by counsel or speech
medium.explanation: The chapter describes the effects of righteousness, gossip, counsel, provision, and wicked speech on the city.
medium.q: How does a person’s conduct affect society in this chapter?

medium.explanation: The lowly are humble, and they are associated with wisdom rather than shame.
medium.q: In the chapter, what does “lowly” describe?

answers: They produce benefit and blessing beyond the individual
They isolate a person from society
challenge.explanation: Integrity delivers, generosity refreshes, and seeking good procures favour.
challenge.q: What principle is shared by integrity, generosity, and seeking good?

answers: Character, wisdom, and righteousness matter more
The chapter says nothing about character
challenge.explanation: The chapter values discretion, wisdom, righteousness, and integrity above beauty or trust in riches.
challenge.q: How does the chapter compare inner character with outward possessions or appearance?

answers: People ultimately face fitting consequences for their deeds
The righteous and wicked always share the same end
challenge.explanation: The chapter presents deliverance and life for the righteous, but shame, falling, and punishment for the wicked.
challenge.q: What is the chapter’s overall message about recompense?
